name: Bergruhe
title: Overview
text: An interactive 3D Alpine cabin by Andre Parrocho: charred larch, a concrete base set into the slope, a diagonal roof, a glass room cantilevered over the valley, a hearth column, sauna and hot tub. Third of the Design Studies.

name: Bergruhe
title: Massing
text: The timber volume over its concrete base. Living is on the valley side, two storeys high. Bedrooms are at the back on two floors.

name: Bergruhe
title: Roof: the signature
text: The diagonal roof is Bergruhe’s signature, one long line rising toward the view. The horizontal roof trades it for a deep flat slab that has to carry the full snow load. The classic gable is there to compare against.

name: Bergruhe
title: Lower level
text: In the concrete base. The sauna opens onto the terrace and the front east room is storage. The garage takes the middle of the level, behind the hearth base, with a side door reached by a drive cut into the slope.

name: Bergruhe
title: Altitude
text: Altitude sets the design snow load in Particulars.

name: Bergruhe
title: Scene & season
text: Time of day, snow and weather. These don’t change the design. Deeper snow means a lower winter sun and shorter days.

name: Denkraum
title: Overview
text: An interactive 3D studio by Andre Parrocho: Denkraum, a 42 m² room for design and real estate work high in a Manila tower, built around a concrete vault that keeps client deeds, drawings and data. Fourth of the Design Studies.

name: Denkraum
title: Room
text: One tight room of about 30 to 50 m² on the corner of a high floor. Glass on two sides, the vault wall at the back.

name: Denkraum
title: The vault: the signature
text: Clients trust you with deeds, drawings and data, so they never leave this wall. Half a metre of reinforced concrete with a two-hour fire rating, a wall of locking drawers, and a vault room behind a round door with the servers inside.

name: Denkraum
title: Zones
text: Five places in one room: make, meet, present, read and rest.

name: Denkraum
title: Tech
text: Everything runs here, and nothing goes to the cloud. The vault has its own cooling and battery.

name: Denkraum
title: Quiet & hidden
text: A box inside a box: a floating floor, a lining on springs and laminated double glass. The way in is a door you can’t see.

name: Denkraum
title: Typhoon & heat
text: Built for Manila: heat all year, monsoon rain and Signal No. 5 winds.

name: Denkraum
title: Arrival
text: Two lifts run from the garage under the plaza straight into a private lobby beside the studio. Heimweg charges in its space below.

name: Denkraum
title: Scene & weather
text: Time of day, weather and the light inside. These don’t change the design. The sun rises over the glass.

name: Durchfahrt
title: Overview
text: An interactive design study by Andre Parrocho: Durchfahrt, an all-electric bullet train that runs non-stop across the Philippine archipelago, from Luzon down the Visayas to Mindanao. Cars slip off at speed and pods latch on while it moves, and when a typhoon shuts down air and sea travel its stripes turn orange and it becomes the country's lifeline. Seventh of the Design Studies.

name: Fernweh
title: Overview
text: An interactive 3D explorer yacht by Andre Parrocho: sail-assist wing sails, a beach-club garage, a limousine tender and day-to-night scenes. Sister study to das Zuhause.

name: Fernweh
title: Hull
text: The explorer hull, with a high bow, deep freeboard and long range.

name: Fernweh
title: Decks
text: Stacked levels, with the owner’s suite at the top and a glass sky lounge above it.

name: Fernweh
title: Explorer kit
text: The gear that makes it an expedition boat.

name: Fernweh
title: Top deck: wings or helipad
text: Choose what defines Fernweh. Wing sails are computer-turned sail-assist wings that ease off long before the boat would heel and furl to bare masts for typhoons. The helipad sits on top of the sky lounge. A real owner picks one, because rotor blades and 30 m wings can’t share the sky.

name: Fernweh
title: Scene & sea
text: Time of day, sea state and the horizon. These don’t change the design.

name: Geborgenheit
title: Overview
text: An interactive 3D sanctuary by Andre Parrocho: Geborgenheit, a retreat carved into the wall of a river gorge in the Bukidnon highlands, Mindanao, with an underground garden under a light well, a vault, and enough stored food, river water and river power to shelter a family for about a year. Fifth of the Design Studies.

name: Geborgenheit
title: The gorge
text: Set into the north wall of a river gorge in the Bukidnon highlands, Mindanao. The rooms sit 10 m above the river, clear of its worst floods, with the plateau far overhead.

name: Geborgenheit
title: The heart: garden and light well
text: An underground garden under a light well cut up through the rock. A thin waterfall runs down one wall, and after dark the well frames the night sky.

name: Geborgenheit
title: The vault
text: Beside the garden: art and books, memories and essentials. A memory wall leads to its door.

name: Geborgenheit
title: Rooms
text: Carved out of the rock along the river, each one with a reason to be there.

name: Geborgenheit
title: A year on its own
text: Stored food, garden greens, river water and river power. In an emergency it shelters the family for about a year.

name: Geborgenheit
title: Arrival
text: Heimweg parks in a hidden bay on the plateau and charges from the river. A glass lift, like das Zuhause’s glass core, runs down the gorge wall; then a lantern path runs along the water to the door.

name: Geborgenheit
title: Scene & weather
text: Time of day, weather and what is open. These don’t change the design. The gorge runs east to west, so the sun crosses over the light well.

name: Heimweg
title: Overview
text: Heimweg, an original electric luxury off-roader by Andre Parrocho: a 2.75 m tall minimal monolith on big tyres under flared arches, with a glass canopy, a warm light signature, and camp mode with an awning, a pop-up roof and a pull-out kitchen. The first of the Models.

name: Heimweg
title: Body & stance
text: One calm block standing 2.75 m tall on 1.2 m tyres. The lower body is tough and matte, step boards help you up, and the air suspension lifts it for deep snow and flood water.

name: Heimweg
title: Glass canopy
text: One continuous sheet of glass from windscreen to tailgate. Dim it dark for privacy or clear it to see the cabin.

name: Heimweg
title: Light signature
text: A hairline of light across the full width at the front. At the back, a vertical lamp on each rear corner faces the traffic behind you and wraps onto the side. They work as tail lights, brake lights (with a third light high on the tailgate), sequential amber turn signals and reversing lights. Try each one below, or press Welcome home to see them sweep.

name: Heimweg
title: Expedition kit
text: Carried on the side-hinged tailgate, so it all swings out of the way with the boot.

name: Sternweh
title: Overview
text: An interactive 3D design study by Andre Parrocho: Sternweh, a home under the stars and a pilgrimage, one great glass dome sunk into the Atacama Desert in Chile so that only its glass shows above the ground. You arrive only at night, on foot, guided by low lights. Sixth of the Design Studies.

name: Sternweh
title: The dome
text: One dome sunk into the desert, so only its glass shows above the ground. The glass is laminated and walkable, in a fine steel grid that can move in an earthquake.

name: Sternweh
title: The three hearts
text: The sky court, the sleeping chamber and the star room, all under the glass.

name: Sternweh
title: Rooms under the glass
text: Warm wood and textiles. There are no lamps here: at night the stars light these rooms, with tiny amber markers on the steps. By day a woven textile is drawn under the glass to hold the sun’s heat up against it.

name: Sternweh
title: Hallways and kitchen
text: The only rooms with solid ceilings: classical panelled hallways in a ring round the dome, and the kitchen below them beside the white studio. Lit by lamps and floor uplights only, with one spotlight over the kitchen island.

name: Sternweh
title: Arrival
text: Heimweg stops out in the desert and you walk the last stretch at night, guided by low amber lights. Then it drives itself down a hidden ramp into its showroom.

name: Sternweh
title: Off the grid
text: Solar panels far out in the desert, fog catchers on the hills toward the sea, an underground cistern, and the RV beside Heimweg as a water reserve.

name: Sternweh
title: Sky & scene
text: Time, season, moon and weather. These don’t change the design. Sternweh lies at 24.6° south, so the bright core of the Milky Way passes overhead on winter nights.

name: das Zuhause
title: Overview
text: A residence study in tropical brutalism with mid-century and Japanese influences. You arrive by the lit stone stair from photo IMG_8572.

name: das Zuhause
title: The approach
text: The wide stair and tall entrance from your photo.

name: das Zuhause
title: Massing
text: A glazed mid-century pavilion with a concrete bar cantilevered above it.

name: das Zuhause
title: Roof
text: A thin floating slab with deep eaves for tropical sun and rain.

name: das Zuhause
title: Facade
text: Shade and airflow, the tropical way.

name: das Zuhause
title: Garden
text: A Japanese courtyard with a lap pool behind the house, and a koi pond in front.

name: das Zuhause
title: Cistern
text: Rainwater from the roofs is filtered, then stored in a brutalist concrete hall under the plinth. Its cool air also ventilates the house. Open the Underground view to see it.

name: das Zuhause
title: Cistern definition
text: A cistern is a tank that stores water.
